title: k8s-rag-operator-gke-quickstart: operator-based RAG deployment + tool-binding samples
author: Maya Chen
description:
Motivation: Provide a compact, production-minded quickstart that demonstrates how to run a RAG-style agent on Kubernetes using an operator pattern tailored for GKE. Many teams run agents as single pods in examples which misses realistic concerns: lifecycle for indexers/retrievers, rolling updates for model variants, and safe tool-binding (external connectors) configuration. This PR introduces a lightweight k8s operator-style quickstart, CRDs, sample Helm hooks, and curated examples for tool-calling (GCS + Pub/Sub) so teams can adopt operator-managed RAG deployments in their clusters with minimal plumbing.

What this PR adds (high level): single continuous README and step-by-step quickstart docs; a small operator manifest and Helm chart fragment to manage three CRDs (Retriever, Indexer, Agent); sample kustomize overlay for GKE with Workload Identity hints; sample Agent CR that wires a Retriever and an Indexer; two tool-binding examples showing safe tool credentials mounting and webhook proxies (GCS uploader and Pub/Sub notifier); local dev notes (minikube / kind) and an Authoring checklist to validate streaming and structured-output behavior.

Key files changed: quickstarts/k8s-rag-operator/README.md — full quickstart walkthrough and troubleshooting; quickstarts/k8s-rag-operator/crds/agent.crd.yaml, retriever.crd.yaml, indexer.crd.yaml — CRD definitions; helm/charts/rag-operator/templates/deployment.yaml — operator deployment (small, single-replica controller by default); examples/gke/operator/sample-agent.yaml — sample Agent CR wiring tool bindings; examples/gke/operator/tool-bindings/gcs-uploader.yaml and pubsub-notifier.yaml — concrete tool binding manifests and secrets examples (Workload Identity notes included); docs/quickstarts/k8s-operator.md — docs site page that will be picked up by the docs pipeline and linked from the quickstarts index; scripts/local-dev/kind-setup.sh — small convenience script for running the quickstart locally.

Commits (summary): ["init: quickstart scaffold and README (quickstarts/k8s-rag-operator)", "crd: add Agent/Retriever/Indexer CRD schema and validation hints", "helm: add rag-operator chart and sample values for GKE", "examples: add GCS/ PubSub tool-binding manifests and notes", "docs: add docs/quickstarts/k8s-operator.md and link to quickstart index", "test: add smoketest that deploys sample Agent to kind in CI (skips on PRs from forks)"]

Testing and CI: Added a lightweight smoketest job that runs a kind cluster, applies the CRDs and the operator, and deploys the sample Agent with a stubbed retriever that returns a deterministic small index. The smoketest checks: CRD registration, operator pod reaches Ready, sample Agent becomes Available, and a single evaluation request path returns a structured JSON output that includes a tool call stub entry. The smoketest is marked as optional on forks to avoid secrets leaks. Initial CI run flagged a timing flake where controller probe intervals were too long; fixed by shortening readiness probe backoff in a follow-up commit. Final CI status: pass.

Review notes and tradeoffs: The operator in this quickstart is intentionally minimal — it does not implement heavy autoscaling logic or advanced rollout strategies. Instead it demonstrates the Operator pattern to manage RAG components (indexer, retriever, agent) and surface where platform teams would plug Redwood Dedicated/Private endpoints and model variants. Security: examples recommend GKE Workload Identity for credentials; the GCS and Pub/Sub examples use placeholder IAM bindings and document required IAM roles rather than embedding secrets. Backwards compatibility: this quickstart is additive and does not change any existing API surfaces.

How to run locally (short): 1) git clone && cd quickstarts/k8s-rag-operator; 2) ./scripts/local-dev/kind-setup.sh (creates kind cluster with CRDs); 3) helm install ./helm/charts/rag-operator --namespace redwood-rag; 4) kubectl apply -f examples/gke/operator/sample-agent.yaml; 5) kubectl port-forward svc/rag-agent 8080:8080 and run the smoke curl provided in README to exercise tool-calling flow. Full runbook and troubleshooting are in the README.

Rollout & docs: docs/quickstarts/k8s-operator.md was added and linked from the quickstarts index page; the docs page contains a compatibility table that maps quickstart concepts to Redwood product surfaces (Hosted API, Dedicated, Private) and includes SLO/cost notes for running retrievers as sidecars vs. centralized services.

Checklist (completed): [x] Quickstart README + runbook [x] CRDs + minimal operator controller manifest [x] Helm chart fragment and values [x] Tool-binding examples (GCS, PubSub) with security notes [x] Local dev script and CI smoketest [x] Docs site page and quickstarts index link

Release notes: Adds a GKE-focused quickstart demonstrating an operator approach for RAG deployments, including safe tool-binding patterns and sample manifests for GCS and Pub/Sub connectors. Useful for platform teams and customers migrating from single-pod examples to operator-managed deployments.

Follow-ups (planned): add optional autoscaler integration for Dedicated pools, and a sample rollout policy that switches model variants with canary traffic.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-3982 (k8s operator quickstart), PM-214 (quickstart prioritization), SUP-1123 (customer request for GKE docs).

review_comments: Liam O'Connor: Nice focused quickstart — two small asks: 1) can we document the minimum RBAC roles needed for Workload Identity in the README? 2) In the operator deployment, prefer a single liveness probe endpoint to avoid flapping in slow CI.
Maya Chen (author): Addressed both: added RBAC section with minimal IAM bindings and switched liveness probe to /healthz. Also shortened readiness probe backoff which fixed the smoketest flake.
Priya Nair: Approving once we clarify the docs note about 'indexer persistence' — please call out that the example uses an ephemeral in-memory index for dev only.

Maya Chen: Good catch — added a dedicated paragraph in README and the docs page about production persistence options (GCS-backed indices, BigTable, or dedicated vector DB) and how to wire them into the Indexer CR.
Dmitri Volkov: CI looked good; small nit about helm values naming — changed values.example.yaml to use explicit serviceAccount.name so GKE WI is clearer.
release_notes: Add a Kubernetes operator quickstart for RAG deployments on GKE with sample tool bindings (GCS, Pub/Sub). Includes CRDs, Helm fragment, local dev scripts, and docs site page.
notes_for_merger: Squash-merge. No feature flags required. The quickstart is additive. Run docs build locally to confirm table of contents entry before merging. CI smoketest must be green.
